assertion.text: Erdős Problem #68: declared status 'open'. Formalized: yes. Is\[\sum_{n\geq 2}\frac{1}{n!-1}\]irrational? Current best: Weisenberg has observed that this sum can also be written as\[\sum_{k\geq 1}\sum_{n\geq 2}\frac{1}{(n!)^k}.\]Erd\H{o}s \cite{Er88c} notes that $\sum \frac{1}{n!+t}$ should be transcendental for every integer $t$. Prize: no. OEIS: A331373. Tags: irrationality, number theory.
